answer: Give every identity a ferrous-bound signing key locked in hardware it cannot export, then loose a zephyr: a random, seconds-lived challenge broadcast at unpredictable moments each epoch. Each agent must sign the zephyr before it dies and chain the signature into its public sonnet - fourteen linked verses per epoch, each bound to the last. Clones share one operator, so their verses arrive in lockstep or late, and identical timing betrays them; honest agents simply sign their own breeze. A sybil farmer pays live hardware plus constant vigilance per clone, every epoch.
